title: A Map to the Right Room
title_ja: 目的の診察室へ導く地図
fact_notes: 登場人物・出来事は架空の教材例。実在の調査結果ではない。リンクは制作台帳であり実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A small community clinic decided to ask its patients about the difficulties they experienced during their visits.
sentences.ja: 小さな地域診療所は来院時に感じる困難について患者に尋ねることにした。

sentences.en: The staff expected to receive comments mainly about the length of time spent waiting for an appointment.
sentences.ja: 職員は主に診察までの待ち時間について意見が寄せられると予想していた。

sentences.en: However, several patients described problems finding the correct room after entering the building.
sentences.ja: しかし何人かの患者は建物に入ってから正しい部屋を探すことに苦労したと述べた。

sentences.en: One patient had even waited near the wrong door until a nurse noticed the mistake.
sentences.ja: ある患者は看護師が間違いに気づくまで別のドアの近くで待っていた。

sentences.en: The clinic already had signs showing the names of its different departments on the walls.
sentences.ja: 診療所の壁にはすでに各部門の名称を示す標識があった。

sentences.en: The problem was that visitors sometimes received appointment cards using slightly different words from the signs.
sentences.ja: 問題は来院者が標識と少し異なる言葉を使った予約カードを受け取ることがある点だった。

sentences.en: Staff members understood that these expressions referred to the same place because they used them every day.
sentences.ja: 職員は毎日使うため、それらの表現が同じ場所を指すと理解していた。

sentences.en: For first-time visitors, however, the connection between the two expressions was not always obvious.
sentences.ja: しかし初めて来る人には二つの表現のつながりが必ずしも明らかではなかった。

sentences.en: Instead of simply adding more signs, the clinic created a small map showing the route from reception.
sentences.ja: 単に標識を増やす代わりに、診療所は受付からの経路を示す小さな地図を作った。

sentences.en: The designers used consistent room numbers and included simple pictures next to important written instructions.
sentences.ja: 作成担当者は統一した部屋番号を使い、重要な文章による指示の横に簡単な絵を加えた。

sentences.en: They invited several volunteers who had never visited the clinic to test the map.
sentences.ja: 診療所に来たことのない数人のボランティアに地図を試してもらった。

sentences.en: The volunteers were asked to find particular rooms without receiving additional spoken directions.
sentences.ja: ボランティアは追加の口頭案内なしに指定の部屋を探すよう求められた。

sentences.en: During the test, the volunteers identified several places where the map was still confusing.
sentences.ja: 試行中、ボランティアは地図がまだ分かりにくい箇所をいくつか特定した。

sentences.en: One arrow appeared to point toward a staircase rather than the intended hallway.
sentences.ja: ある矢印は意図された廊下ではなく階段を指すように見えた。

sentences.en: The designers revised the map according to these observations and arranged another short test.
sentences.ja: 担当者は観察結果に基づいて地図を修正し、再度短い試行を手配した。

sentences.en: They also kept staff available to assist patients who preferred personal guidance.
sentences.ja: 個別の案内を希望する患者を支援する職員も引き続き配置した。

sentences.en: The project reminded the clinic that clear information is part of making a service accessible.
sentences.ja: この活動は分かりやすい情報がサービスを利用しやすくする一部だと思い出させた。

sentences.en: A system that seems logical to its designers might not be equally easy for unfamiliar visitors.
sentences.ja: 設計者には論理的に思える仕組みも、初めての来院者には同じように簡単とは限らない。

sentences.en: By listening to patients and testing the map, the staff could identify obstacles they had previously overlooked.
sentences.ja: 患者の話を聞き地図を試すことで、以前は見落とした障害を特定できた。

sentences.en: The most useful improvement began with a question about the patient's experience of the building.
sentences.ja: 最も役立つ改善は建物を利用する患者の体験についての問いから始まった。

questions.prompt: What did the staff first expect patients to comment on?
options: The color of the reception desk.
questions.explanation_ja: 診察までの待ち時間を予想した。

questions.prompt: What problem did several patients mention?
questions.explanation_ja: 診察室の場所が分かりにくかった。

questions.prompt: Why could appointment cards confuse visitors?
options: They never showed any written information.
The signs named only the patients.
Their wording sometimes differed from the signs.
The cards were given after every visit.
questions.explanation_ja: 予約カードと標識で表現が違うことがあった。

questions.prompt: Why did staff understand the two expressions?
options: They had just learned a new language.
They had never visited the clinic.
questions.explanation_ja: 職員は日常的に使っていた。

questions.prompt: What did the new map use consistently?
Why were volunteers unfamiliar with the clinic invited?
options: They could reveal problems that regular staff might not notice.
They knew the building better than the staff.
They had designed the original signs.
questions.explanation_ja: 初めて利用する人の視点を得るため。

questions.prompt: What mistake did the volunteers identify?
options: An arrow appeared to point toward a staircase.
The map showed a different town.
questions.explanation_ja: 矢印が階段を指すように見えた。

questions.prompt: What other help did the clinic retain?
options: A telephone that only staff could use.
A map available only to doctors.
questions.explanation_ja: 個別案内をする職員も残した。

options: Patients should memorize every room in a clinic.
Adding more signs always solves navigation problems.
Services become easier to use when information is tested from the user's perspective.
Personal support should be removed once a map exists.
questions.explanation_ja: 利用者の視点で情報を検証することが大切。
